findings.note: FAQ item 3 ('Possibly. State law lists conditions that can make a building substandard, such as junk and debris that are fire, health or safety hazards...') states the listed conditions without the threshold 'to an extent that endangers the life, limb, health, property, safety, or welfare of the occupants of the building, nearby residents, or the public' (clm:8, H&S 17920.3 opening paragraph). clm:1 is labelled NARROWER only because every citing unit cites clm:8; this item does not. A reader would believe junk and debris alone can make a building substandard. Reader impact: changes. Also the item cites clm:2, clm:3, clm:4 but its text uses none of them.

FAQ item 3: 'The statute does not mention hoarding.' is an absence-of-law claim. The ledger has no statute_absence claim for it (SR-6). Remove the sentence, or have Research record a statute_absence claim with the full official text read and the section and date, then cite it.

FAQ item 4 ('Who can sell the house if the owner cannot or will not?') cites no claim yet states a list of legal roles ('the owner, a trustee, an executor or administrator, or several heirs who agree'), a rule ('Only someone with legal authority to sign') and a case-specific legal conclusion ('Living in the house alone does not give you that authority'). None is supported by the ledger. Rewrite without the role list and without the conclusion, for example: who can sign depends on how title is held and on the family's situation; confirm with an attorney or title company. Or have Research add a sourced claim for it.

FAQ item 2 opens 'Not always.' to 'Do I have to clean out a house before selling it?' This implies that cleanout is sometimes required, and no claim supports that. 'a direct buyer prices in the condition' is also uncited, though it matches the brief's sell_directly option and states no legal rule. Plainer wording would help, for example 'No law in this guide requires it; it depends on your time, money and route.' Only use that if the wording is checked against a source. Otherwise say 'It depends on...'.

required_actions: Item 3: cite clm:8 and state the threshold in the answer ('to an extent that endangers the life, limb, health, property, safety, or welfare of occupants, nearby residents or the public'). Say a local official decides, or name the deciders, without a closed list.
Item 3: delete 'The statute does not mention hoarding.' unless a statute_absence claim is added to the ledger.
Item 4: remove the unsupported role list and 'Living in the house alone does not give you that authority', or support them with a ledger claim. Keep the confirm-with-attorney-or-title-company line.
